## Website Speed Optimization Price: Scope Tiers, Real Measurements and Score-Only Traps
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-speed-optimisation-charges
Updated: 2026-11-03
Short answer: A website speed optimization price should pay for measured improvements in how fast real visitors see and use your pages, not just a higher PageSpeed score. Cost depends on the platform, hosting, number of heavy plugins and images, and whether the theme itself is slow. Ongoing speed monitoring is part of maintenance from Rs 7,200 a month.
Key points:
- Pay for improvements in real loading and interaction, measured before and after, not a score screenshot.
- Core Web Vitals (loading, responsiveness and visual stability) are the measures Google itself describes.
- Quick wins such as image compression and caching cost little; heavy themes and page builders cost more to fix.
- Hosting matters; no optimisation can fully hide a slow or overloaded server.
- Sometimes a lighter rebuild is cheaper than repeated speed work on a bloated site.

Q: What should a website speed optimization service include?
A: It should include measuring key pages on mobile before work, fixing the main causes such as heavy images, missing caching, unused plugins and slow scripts, testing forms and payments afterwards, and a before-and-after report showing Core Web Vitals and real-user data where available.

Q: Is a PageSpeed score of 90 or more worth paying for?
A: A score is a useful signal but not the goal. Some services raise the lab score with tricks that do not help visitors or break features. Pay for faster loading and interaction for real users, measured in Core Web Vitals field data, with all site features still working.

Q: What are Core Web Vitals?
A: They are three measures Google describes for page experience: Largest Contentful Paint for loading speed, Interaction to Next Paint for responsiveness and Cumulative Layout Shift for visual stability. PageSpeed Insights shows them for your pages, including data from real visitors when enough exist.

Q: Can better hosting make my website faster?
A: Often, yes. A slow or overloaded shared server makes every page slow, however well the site is optimised. Checking server response time is one of the first steps, and moving to better hosting or adding a content delivery network is sometimes the cheapest single improvement.

Q: Why is speed work on page-builder sites more expensive?
A: Heavy themes and page builders add a lot of code, scripts and styles to every page. Quick fixes help a little, but bigger gains often need replacing key templates or the theme itself, which takes more time. Sometimes a lighter rebuild costs less than repeated optimisation.

Q: How much does website speed optimization cost with Kamboh Associates?
A: We quote after measuring your key pages, because the platform, theme, plugins, images and hosting decide the work. Ongoing speed monitoring and small fixes are part of maintenance from Rs 7,200 a month. A lighter rebuild uses our starter package at Rs 40,500 or business package at Rs 85,500.

Q: Website ki speed barhane ke liye kis cheez ke paise dene chahiye?
A: Sirf PageSpeed score ke liye nahi, balke asal users ke liye page ke jaldi khulne aur chalne ke liye. Kaam se pehle aur baad mobile par Core Web Vitals ki report maangein, aur check karein ke forms, payment aur WhatsApp button kaam kar rahe hain. Hosting bhi check karwayein.

## Website Migration Cost: Moving to a New Host or a New Platform Without Breaking Things
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-migration-charges
Updated: 2026-11-03
Short answer: Website migration cost depends mainly on what moves. Moving a small site to a new host is usually a short, low-risk job. Moving platforms, such as WooCommerce to Shopify, involves products, customers, orders, URLs and redirects, and takes much longer. Risk items such as email, payments and SEO need testing. Store rebuilds start at Rs 157,500.
Key points:
- Host moves keep the same site; platform moves rebuild it elsewhere, which costs far more.
- The risk items are email, DNS, payments, forms, SEO redirects and customer accounts.
- Agree the scope in writing: what data moves, what is rebuilt and what is tested.
- A full backup before the move and a testing checklist after it protect you from losses.
- Plan the switch-over for a quiet time and keep the old setup running until the new one is confirmed.

Q: What is the difference between a host migration and a platform migration?
A: A host migration moves the same website to a new hosting company, so it looks and works the same afterwards. A platform migration moves the business to different software, such as WooCommerce to Shopify, which is effectively a rebuild with data transfer and costs much more.

Q: What can go wrong when migrating a website?
A: Email can stop if MX records are not copied, HTTPS may fail, payment gateways may need new credentials, forms and order emails often break, changed URLs without redirects lose rankings, and customer passwords usually cannot move between platforms. Each needs planning and testing.

Q: How do I avoid losing SEO during a platform migration?
A: Map every old URL to its new equivalent and set up 301 redirects, keep page titles and content where possible, submit the new sitemap, and watch Search Console for errors in the weeks after launch. Google's site move documentation explains the full process.

Q: Can customer accounts be moved to a new store platform?
A: Customer names, emails, addresses and order history can usually be imported, but passwords normally cannot be moved, because platforms store them in encrypted form. Plan to send customers a friendly invitation to reset their password on the new store after the switch.

Q: What should a website migration quote include?
A: It should list what data moves, what is rebuilt, which integrations are reconnected, who handles DNS and email, the backup before work starts, the testing checklist, the switch-over date and how long the old site stays live. Without this, costs and risks are unclear.

Q: How much does a website migration cost?
A: A small host move is usually a short job, often included for clients on maintenance from Rs 7,200 a month. Platform migrations are priced like a new build plus data transfer, starting from our store package at Rs 157,500 for online stores and our business package at Rs 85,500 for business sites.

Q: Website ko nayi hosting ya platform par shift karne ka kharcha kitna hai?
A: Agar sirf hosting badalni hai to aam tor par chhota kaam hai. Agar platform badalna hai, jaise WooCommerce se Shopify, to products, customers, orders, URLs aur redirects sab muntaqil hote hain aur kharcha zyada hai. Pehle poora backup lein aur shift ke baad email, payment aur forms test karein.

- Most domain losses happen because renewal notices go to an old email address or a former developer.

## SSL Certificate Price in Pakistan: When Free Is Enough and When Paid Makes Sense
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/ssl-certificate-price-pakistan
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: For most business websites in Pakistan, the SSL certificate price is zero: free certificates from Let's Encrypt, often installed automatically by the host or by Cloudflare, give the same encryption as paid ones. Paid organisation or extended validation certificates add identity checks, which a small number of businesses need. Renewal every 90 days should be automatic.
Key points:
- Free and paid SSL certificates encrypt traffic in the same way; the difference is how much identity checking is done.
- Let's Encrypt issues free certificates that renew automatically, and many hosts install them for you.
- Paid OV and EV certificates verify the organisation, which some banks, payment partners or tenders may require.
- Never pay a host yearly for a basic certificate that the same host can install free.
- The real risk is an expired certificate; make sure renewal is automatic and monitored.

Q: Is a free SSL certificate safe for an online store in Pakistan?
A: Yes. A free Let's Encrypt certificate gives the same encryption strength as a paid one, and browsers show the same padlock. Online stores, payment pages and forms run safely on free certificates, provided they renew automatically and the whole site loads over HTTPS.

Q: How often does a free SSL certificate need renewing?
A: Let's Encrypt certificates are valid for 90 days and are designed to renew automatically before they expire. Most hosting control panels and services such as Cloudflare handle renewal without any action. Monitoring should still warn you if a renewal ever fails.

Q: What is the difference between DV, OV and EV certificates?
A: A domain-validated certificate only confirms control of the domain. An organisation-validated certificate also checks the business's legal details, and an extended validation certificate involves more detailed checks. All three encrypt traffic the same way; they differ in the identity checking behind them.

Q: Should I pay my hosting company for an SSL certificate?
A: Usually not for a basic certificate. Ask whether the host supports free Let's Encrypt certificates with automatic renewal. If it charges yearly for something it could install free, or does not support free certificates at all, consider moving to better hosting.

Q: What happens if my SSL certificate expires?
A: Browsers show a full-page security warning and most visitors leave immediately. Payments and forms may stop working. Expiry usually follows a failed automatic renewal, often after hosting or DNS changes, so monitoring that checks certificate expiry is worth setting up.

Q: Do websites built by Kamboh Associates Digital include SSL?
A: Yes. Every site we build launches on HTTPS with a free certificate that renews automatically, with HTTP redirected to HTTPS and mixed content fixed. Sites on our maintenance plan from Rs 7,200 a month are also monitored for certificate problems.

Q: Website ke liye SSL certificate ki qeemat kitni hai?
A: Zyada tar websites ke liye SSL muft hai. Let's Encrypt ka free certificate wohi hifazat deta hai jo paid deta hai, aur hosting aksar khud laga deti hai. Paid OV ya EV certificate sirf tab lein jab koi bank, payment partner ya tender is ki shart rakhe.

## Business Email Price in Pakistan per User: Google Workspace, Zoho and Hosting Mail
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/business-email-price-per-user-pakistan
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: The business email price in Pakistan is mostly a per-user monthly or yearly fee: Google Workspace and Zoho Mail charge for each mailbox, listed on their official pricing pages, while hosting mailboxes often come with web hosting. Budget by counting real users; a team of 5 often needs 5 paid users plus free aliases such as info@ and sales@.
Key points:
- Google Workspace and Zoho Mail charge per user; check their official pricing pages for the current rate in your currency.
- An alias or group address such as info@ usually costs nothing extra on top of a paid user.
- Mailboxes included with hosting are cheap but weaker on spam filtering, storage and reliability.
- Yearly plans usually cost less per month than monthly plans, but lock you in for the year.
- Set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC records whatever provider you choose, or emails land in spam.

Q: How is Google Workspace priced for Pakistani businesses?
A: Google Workspace charges a fee per user, billed monthly or yearly, with several plan levels. The current price for Pakistan is shown on Google's official Workspace pricing page, often in rupees. Count only people who need their own mailbox, and use free aliases for shared addresses.

Q: Is Zoho Mail cheaper than Google Workspace?
A: Zoho offers lower-cost mail-only plans, which often makes it cheaper for small teams that only need email. Google Workspace includes more apps such as Drive and Meet. Compare the current per-user prices on both official pricing pages and choose based on what your team will actually use.

Q: Do I need a separate paid user for info@ and sales@?
A: Usually not. Shared addresses can be set up as aliases or groups that deliver to existing paid users at no extra cost. You need a paid user only for each person who sends and receives email under their own name.

Q: Is email included with web hosting good enough for a business?
A: It can work for one or two addresses with low volume. As a business grows, hosting email often suffers from weak spam filtering, small storage and outages whenever the website has problems. Keeping email with a dedicated provider is safer for most businesses.

Q: Which DNS records stop business email landing in spam?
A: The most common reason is missing or wrong SPF, DKIM and DMARC records on your domain. These tell receiving servers that your emails are genuine. Add them for your email provider and check that no old provider's records conflict with the new ones.

Q: Who sets up business email for websites built by Kamboh Associates Digital?
A: We set up domain records, users and aliases at launch if you want email on your domain, with the provider account in your own name. For clients on our maintenance plan from Rs 7,200 a month, routine changes such as adding users are included.

Q: Business email ka kharcha kaise kam karein?
A: Sirf un logon ke liye paid user lein jo apne naam se email bhejte hain. info@ aur sales@ jaise addresses alias bana kar muft chalayein. Company chhorne walon ke account band karein, aur agar team ka size badalta rehta hai to mahana plan lein.

## Website Audit Cost: What a Proper Audit Should Cover and What Free Tools Already Do
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-audit-charges
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Website audit cost depends on site size and how many areas are checked: speed, search, security, accessibility and conversion. A useful audit ends with a prioritised list of fixes, each with its effect and effort, not a long export from a tool. Free tools cover many basics, so pay for the judgement, usually 1 to 3 days of work.
Key points:
- Agree the scope first: which areas are checked and how many page templates are reviewed.
- Free tools such as PageSpeed Insights and Search Console cover many basics; a paid audit should add judgement.
- The deliverable should be a prioritised fix list with effort and expected impact, not a raw tool report.
- Audit the page templates that bring enquiries first: home, services, products and contact.
- Decide in advance whether fixes are included or quoted separately after the audit.

Q: What does a website audit include?
A: A proper audit checks speed and mobile performance, search basics such as indexing, titles and redirects, structured data, security and updates, accessibility, and conversion elements like forms and calls to action. It should end with a prioritised fix list, not just a tool export.

Q: Can I audit my website myself with free tools?
A: You can cover many basics with PageSpeed Insights, Google Search Console, Lighthouse and the Rich Results Test. They show slow pages, indexing issues and missing markup. A paid audit adds judgement about which issues matter for your business and what to fix first.

Q: What should I receive after a paid website audit?
A: You should receive a plain-language summary of the main findings, a prioritised fix list with impact and effort for each item, screenshots or examples, and a clear recommendation to fix, partly rebuild or rebuild. Avoid audits that deliver only hundreds of unprioritised errors.

Q: How long does a website audit take?
A: A small business website with a handful of page templates usually takes one to three days of work, depending on the areas in scope and data access. Large stores or custom web apps take longer. Access to Analytics and Search Console speeds the process up.

Q: Are fixes included in the website audit price?
A: Usually not. Most audits deliver findings and a quote for fixes, so you can choose who carries them out. With us, sites that move to our maintenance plan from Rs 7,200 a month get the most important fixes handled over time.

Q: Should I audit before redesigning my website?
A: If you are unsure whether to fix or rebuild, yes. A focused audit shows whether problems are fixable within the current site or built into its foundations. If you already know a rebuild is needed, spend the budget on planning the new site instead.

Q: Website audit karwane se pehle kya tayyari karein?
A: Google Analytics aur Search Console ka access dein, batayein ke website se aap kya chahte hain jaise calls ya WhatsApp messages, aur haal ki tabdeeliyan bhi batayein. Sab se ahem pages ke naam dein, taa ke audit wahan se shuru ho jahan se enquiries aati hain.

## Website Malware Removal Cost: What a Proper Cleanup Includes and How to Stop a Repeat
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/malware-removal-charges
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Website malware removal cost depends on how deep the infection goes, how many sites share the hosting account, and whether clean backups exist. A proper cleanup removes the malicious code, closes the way in, changes every password and asks Google to review the site. Without those 4 steps, reinfection is common.
Key points:
- The price depends on the depth of the infection, the number of sites on the account and the backups available.
- Deleting visible malware is not enough; the entry point, often an old plugin or a stolen password, must be closed.
- Every password linked to the site should change: admin users, hosting, database, FTP and email.
- If Google shows a warning, the cleanup should include a review request through Search Console.
- Regular updates, backups and monitoring cost far less than repeated cleanups.

Q: How long does it take to clean a hacked website?
A: A simple infection on a small site can often be cleaned within a day once access is available. Deep infections across the database, several sites on one account or missing backups take longer. Google's review of a security warning adds its own waiting time after the cleanup is complete.

Q: Will a security plugin remove malware on its own?
A: A security plugin can detect many known infections and sometimes remove them, but it often misses hidden backdoors and cannot tell you how the attacker got in. Use it as one tool alongside a manual review, password changes and updates, not as the whole cleanup.

Q: Why did my website get hacked again after cleaning?
A: Reinfection usually means the entry point was never closed. Common causes are an outdated or pirated plugin left in place, a backdoor file the cleanup missed, a password that was not changed, or another infected site on the same hosting account.

Q: Should I restore an old backup instead of cleaning the site?
A: A backup helps only if you know it was taken before the infection and you also close the way in. Restoring an infected backup brings the malware back, and restoring a clean one without updates leaves the same weakness open. Check the backup's date against the first signs.

Q: Does malware removal include removing the Google warning?
A: A proper cleanup should include requesting a review in Google Search Console if the site was flagged. The provider can submit the request with a description of the fix, but Google decides when the warning is removed, so nobody can promise an exact time.

Q: What does Kamboh Associates Digital include in a malware cleanup?
A: We copy the infected site, remove malicious code from files and the database, close the entry point, replace the core and plugins from official sources, change passwords and request a Google review if needed. Our maintenance plan from Rs 7,200 a month then keeps the site updated and monitored.

Q: Website hack ho jaye to pehle kya karein?
A: Ghabrayein nahin. Pehle hosting aur admin ke passwords badlein, apne developer ya hosting company ko foran batayein, aur koi file khud delete na karein. Site ki ek copy mehfooz karwayein, phir poori safai karwa kar woh rasta band karwayein jahan se hack hua.

## Product Upload Charges for an Online Store: What a Listing Includes and How It Is Priced
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/product-upload-charges-online-store
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Product upload charges are usually set per item or per batch, and the price depends on what each listing includes: title, description, photos, variants, price, stock and search details. A simple listing with 1 photo costs far less than one with 10 variants and written copy. Always agree the listing checklist first.
Key points:
- Agree exactly what one listing includes before comparing per-item prices.
- Variants such as size and colour multiply the work, so count them, not just products.
- Bulk import from a spreadsheet is cheaper for large catalogues with consistent data.
- Ask for a sample of five finished listings before the full batch is uploaded.
- Clean, consistent product data saves money every time you add new stock later.

Q: How are product uploads priced for a Shopify store?
A: Providers usually charge per product, per variant or per batch of products. The fair price depends on what each listing includes, such as written descriptions, photo editing and variants. Ask for the listing checklist in writing and a sample of five finished products before agreeing to a full batch.

Q: Is bulk import cheaper than uploading products one by one?
A: For large catalogues with consistent data, yes. The products are prepared in a spreadsheet template and imported in one go, then checked. It saves time when products share the same fields, but it still needs a careful review afterwards for prices, variants, images and categories.

## Website Translation to Urdu: How the Cost Is Worked Out and How to Keep Quality High
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-urdu-translation-charges
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Website translation to Urdu is usually priced per word or per page, and the cost depends on who translates, how technical the text is and whether a second person reviews it. Machine output alone is cheap but often reads awkwardly. A typical small site needs 5 to 10 key pages translated, not every page.
Key points:
- Count words on the pages that bring enquiries; translating only those keeps the cost sensible.
- Machine translation is a draft, not a finished page; a fluent human review is the step that matters.
- Urdu pages need right-to-left layout, a readable Nastaliq or Naskh font and separate addresses for search engines.
- Agree a glossary of your brand and product terms before translation starts.
- Translation and website setup are two jobs; ask whether a quote covers both.

Q: Is website translation to Urdu charged per word or per page?
A: Both models exist. Per-word pricing is the most common and the easiest to compare, because it counts the English source text. Per-page pricing suits short, similar pages with a word limit. Ask which pages are included and whether a second fluent reviewer is part of the price.

Q: Is an automatic translation tool enough for Urdu pages?
A: You can use machine output as a first draft, but it should not go live without a fluent human edit. Urdu machine translation often has awkward word order and wrong grammar, which makes a business look careless. Product lists and simple instructions are the safest places to start with a draft.

Q: Which Urdu font is best for a website?
A: Choose a Nastaliq or Naskh web font that is clear on small phone screens and loads quickly. Nastaliq looks traditional and familiar to readers, while Naskh is often easier to read at small sizes. Test the font on real phones before launch, including headings, buttons and forms.

Q: Does an Urdu version of my website help with Google search?
A: It can, when each Urdu page has its own web address and correct language tags, so Google shows it to people searching in Urdu. A translated page that is only switched by a script on one address is harder for search engines to understand and may not appear in results.

Q: Should I translate every page of my website to Urdu?
A: Usually not at first. Translate the pages that bring enquiries, such as home, main services, contact and frequently asked questions. Add more pages once you see Urdu visitors using the site. This keeps the first cost small and focuses the budget where it brings results.

Q: Does Kamboh Associates Digital translate websites into Urdu?
A: We build Urdu and bilingual pages with right-to-left layout, readable fonts and language tags as part of our business website packages from Rs 40,500. Translation is quoted per word after we see your pages, and every key page gets a fluent review before it goes live.

Q: Website ko Urdu mein translate karwane ka sahi tareeqa kya hai?
A: Pehle sirf ahem pages chunein, jaise home, services aur contact. Apne brand aur products ke alfaaz ki fehrist banayein, translator ko live page dikhayein, aur kisi doosre Urdu janne wale se check karwayein. Aakhir mein mobile par font aur layout zaroor dekhein.

URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/hosting-kya-hoti-hai
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Hosting kya hoti hai: yeh woh computer ya server hai jahan aap ki website ki files 24 ghante internet par rakhi jaati hain, taa ke koi bhi kisi bhi waqt website khol sake. - Chhoti business website ke liye achhi shared hosting aam taur par kaafi hoti hai.

Q: Shared hosting aur VPS mein kya farq hai?

Q: Kya sab se sasti hosting lena theek hai?

Q: Hosting renew na karein to kya hoga?
A: Website band ho jaati hai, aur agar email bhi isi hosting par ho to emails bhi ruk jaati hain. Kuch muddat baad hosting company files delete bhi kar sakti hai. Is liye renewal ki tareekh yaad rakhein aur website ka apna backup hamesha alag jagah rakhein.

Q: Kya hosting company badli ja sakti hai?
A: Haan. Website ki files aur database nayi hosting par le ja kar domain ki settings badal di jaati hain. Sahi tareeqe se kiya jaye to website bohat kam waqt ke liye ya bilkul band nahin hoti. Lene se pehle poochh lein ke purani company files aur backup aasani se degi.

## Website vs Facebook Page for a Pakistani Business: Ownership, Reach, Trust and Cost Compared
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-vs-facebook-page
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Website vs Facebook page is not an either-or choice for most businesses. A Facebook page is free and good for reaching followers, but Facebook controls it. A website is yours, appears in Google search and builds trust. Most businesses do best with both, and a basic website starts from Rs 22,500.
Key points:
- A Facebook page is free to create, but Facebook sets the rules, the reach and the layout.
- A website is an asset you own, on your own domain, that you control completely.
- Google search sends customers to websites far more than to Facebook pages.
- A Facebook page is better for updates, community and paid ads; a website is better for detail and trust.
- Use each for what it does best and link them together.

Q: Is a Facebook page enough for a small business?
A: It can be enough to start, especially if you sell mainly to people who already follow you. But Facebook controls the page and limits how many followers see each post, and Google sends far more searchers to websites. Most businesses benefit from adding a simple website once they are established.

Q: Does a website help more than Facebook with Google search?
A: Yes. Google can show a Facebook page for your business name, but a website with clear pages for each service, location and common question can appear for many more searches. That brings customers who have never heard of you, not only those who already know your name.

Q: What happens to my business if my Facebook page is hacked?
A: You may lose access to your followers and messages until Facebook restores the page, which can take weeks. A website on your own domain keeps working and tells customers how to reach you. Use two-step verification and more than one admin on the page.

Q: Should Facebook ads send people to my page or my website?
A: For a specific offer or service, send ads to a focused landing page on your website, where you control the message, form and tracking. Sending ads to the Facebook page suits building followers. Many businesses use both, depending on the goal of each campaign.

Q: Can I build a website from my Facebook page content?
A: Yes. Photos, service descriptions, reviews and common questions from your page are a useful starting point. A website then organises them into clear pages, adds prices, FAQs and contact options, and makes the information easy to find on Google and on phones.

Q: How much does Kamboh Associates Digital charge for a website alongside a Facebook page?
A: Our landing pages start from Rs 22,500 and business websites from Rs 40,500. We link the website and the Facebook page together, register the domain in your own name, and show you how to keep both up to date. Every project starts with a written quote.

## Website vs Google Business Profile Alone: What Each Does Well and Where a Site Adds Value
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-vs-google-business-profile-only
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Website vs Google Business Profile: a free profile is excellent for appearing on Google Maps and in local results with your address, timings, reviews and phone number. It is limited for explaining services, prices and answers in detail. Most local businesses do best with both; a simple website starts from Rs 22,500.
Key points:
- A Google Business Profile is free and is the main way to appear on Google Maps.
- Profiles are strong for address, timings, reviews, photos and calls.
- A profile has little room to explain services, prices, process and frequently asked questions.
- A website can appear for many more searches than your business name and location.
- The two work together: the profile links to the website, and the website confirms the profile's details.

Q: Is a Google Business Profile enough without a website?
A: For a small walk-in business with one simple service, it can be enough to start. Once customers compare services or prices, ask detailed questions, or come from beyond your immediate area, a website answers what the profile cannot and usually brings more enquiries from the same visitors.

Q: Does having a website help my Google Business Profile?
A: A website that shows the same name, address and phone number as your profile, with pages for each service, helps Google understand and trust your business. The profile's website link also lets customers check details before calling. Google's guidance stresses keeping this information accurate and consistent.

Q: Can I take bookings through a Google Business Profile?
A: Some business categories can add booking links or use booking partners in their profile, but options vary. A website gives you full control over booking forms, WhatsApp buttons or online stores, and works for every type of business. Many businesses link the profile's booking button to their website.

Q: Why does my profile only show up for my business name?
A: Profiles mostly appear for your name and for local searches matching your category and location. To appear for more detailed searches, such as a specific service or question, you need content that explains it, which is what service pages and FAQs on a website provide.

Q: Should the website and profile show the same details?
A: Yes. Use the same business name, address or service area, phone number and opening hours on both. Inconsistent details confuse customers and make it harder for Google to trust the information. Update both together whenever timings, numbers or locations change.

Q: Does Kamboh Associates Digital set up Google Business Profiles with websites?
A: Yes. We set up or tidy your Google Business Profile in your own Google account alongside the website, so details match. Landing pages start from Rs 22,500 and business websites from Rs 40,500, with the domain registered in your name.

- The page usually lives on the tool's address, not your own domain.
- Link pages rarely bring visitors from Google and offer little space for detail.
- A simple landing page on your own domain can do the same job and grow with you.

Q: Is Linktree enough for a small business?
A: It can be enough at the start, especially for creators or businesses that sell almost entirely through one social platform. As you grow, its limits show: the page sits on the tool's domain, rarely appears on Google and has little room for prices, policies and product details.

Q: Can I use my own domain for a link-in-bio page?
A: Some link-in-bio tools allow a custom domain on paid plans, which helps with branding. A simple landing page on your own domain does the same job and gives you more control over design, content and search visibility, so it is worth comparing both options.

Q: Do link-in-bio pages help with Google search?
A: Rarely. A page that is mostly a list of buttons gives search engines little to understand. To appear for searches about your products or services, you need pages with real descriptions, prices and answers, which a website or detailed landing page provides.

Q: What should I put on my Instagram bio link instead?
A: A landing page on your own domain works well: a short introduction, main products or services, prices or starting prices, delivery or booking details, a WhatsApp button and links to your social profiles. It looks professional and can grow into a full website later.

Q: When should I move from a link page to a full website?
A: Move when you sell regularly, customers search for your products on Google, the same questions keep coming in chat, or you run ads and want a page you control. Many businesses reach this point within a year of starting on social media.

## WhatsApp Catalogue vs Website Store: Product Limits, Checkout and Being Found
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/whatsapp-catalogue-vs-online-store
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: WhatsApp catalogue vs website: the free WhatsApp Business catalogue lets customers browse products inside a chat, which suits small ranges and repeat buyers. A website store adds search visibility, a cart, checkout, stock control and order records. Many sellers start with the catalogue and add a store from Rs 157,500 as orders grow.
Key points:
- The WhatsApp Business catalogue is free and lets you show products with photos and prices inside the app.
- Ordering still happens in chat, which works for small volumes but takes time as orders grow.
- Catalogue items are mostly seen by people already chatting with you, not new customers searching Google.
- A website store adds a cart, checkout, stock tracking, policies and search visibility.
- The two work well together: link the store from WhatsApp and add WhatsApp buttons to the store.

Q: Is the WhatsApp Business catalogue free?
A: Yes. The catalogue is part of the free WhatsApp Business app and lets you list products or services with photos, prices, descriptions and links. Customers can browse it from your profile or a chat. Ordering and payment are still arranged in the conversation, not through a built-in checkout.

Q: Can customers find my WhatsApp catalogue on Google?
A: Generally not in the way they find website product pages. The catalogue is mostly seen by people who already have your number or are chatting with you. To reach new customers searching on Google, you need product pages on a website with real descriptions and prices.

Q: When is a WhatsApp catalogue better than a website store?

Q: How do I know if chat ordering is costing me too much time?
A: For one week, note the minutes spent on each order from first message to confirmed delivery details, then multiply by daily orders. If confirming sizes, addresses and payment takes a large part of the day, a store with checkout will usually pay for itself in time saved.

## Free Hosting vs Paid Hosting for a Business Website: Ads, Limits, Security and Ownership
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/free-hosting-vs-paid-hosting
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Free hosting vs paid hosting: free plans cost nothing upfront but usually add ads, a subdomain, tight limits, weak support and no reliable backups, and the provider can suspend the site at any time. Paid hosting gives you your own domain, speed, security and backups. For a business website, paid hosting is worth it from day 1.
Key points:
- Free hosting often places its own ads or branding on your site and uses a subdomain address.
- Storage, bandwidth and features are limited, and sites can be suspended without warning.
- Security updates and backups are usually weak or absent on free plans.
- Moving away later can be hard if the free host does not let you export your site.
- Good paid hosting is affordable; check renewal prices, backups and support before choosing.

Q: Is free hosting good enough for a small business?
A: Rarely. Free hosting usually adds ads or branding, uses a subdomain address, limits storage and visitors, and offers weak security and backups. The provider can also suspend the site with little notice. For any site that represents your business or takes enquiries, paid hosting is worth it.

Q: Can I use my own domain on free hosting?
A: Some free hosts allow a custom domain, but many restrict it to paid plans or keep their branding on the site. Even with your own domain, the limits on speed, storage, security and support remain. Check the terms carefully before relying on a free plan for a business site.

Q: Why does free hosting show ads on my website?
A: Free hosting providers need to cover their costs, and placing ads or their own branding on your pages is one common way. You usually cannot choose which ads appear, so visitors may see unrelated or even competing businesses. Paid hosting removes third-party ads completely.

Q: What should I check before paying for hosting?
A: Check the renewal price, not only the first-year offer, whether backups are included and easy to restore, whether free SSL is supported, where the servers are located, what support is offered and how easily you can move your files if you leave.

Q: How do I move my website from free hosting to paid hosting?
A: Register your own domain, export the site's files and content if the free host allows it, set the site up on the new hosting, and redirect visitors where possible. If the free builder does not allow export, the site is rebuilt. Plan this before printing the address anywhere.

## Choosing Between .pk vs .com.pk for Your Business Domain, Email and Brand
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/pk-vs-com-pk-domain
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: .pk vs .com.pk: both are Pakistani addresses run by PKNIC, and PKNIC's payment page lists one domain fee for Pakistani registrants, Rs 2,100 a year billed for 2 years (checked 4 November 2026). .pk is shorter and easier for email and branding; .com.pk is familiar for companies. Many businesses register both.
Key points:
- Both .pk and .com.pk are managed by PKNIC, Pakistan's national registry.
- PKNIC's payment page lists one domain fee for registrants in Pakistan rather than separate prices per extension.
- .pk is shorter, which helps on signboards, cards and email addresses.
- .com.pk is long established and familiar for commercial businesses.
- Registering both and redirecting one to the other protects your name for a modest cost.

Q: Is .pk better than .com.pk for a business?
A: Neither is better in search; both are Pakistani extensions run by PKNIC. A .pk address is shorter, which helps on signboards, cards and email, while .com.pk is long established for companies. Choose the one whose name is available and easiest for customers, or register both.

Q: Do .pk and .com.pk have different fees?
A: PKNIC's official payment page lists one domain fee for registrants in Pakistan, Rs 2,100 per year billed two years at a time, rather than separate prices per extension. Check the fee shown in your PKNIC account or invoice for your exact domain. Figures were checked on 4 November 2026.

Q: Should I register both .pk and .com.pk?
A: For an established business, it is often sensible. Choose one as the main address and redirect the other to it with a permanent redirect. This protects your name, catches visitors who type the other version and costs only the extra domain fee. Avoid running two copies of the site.

Q: Which domain should I use for business email?
A: Use only one domain for email, usually your main website domain. A shorter domain such as .pk gives shorter addresses that are easier to spell on the phone. Set up the email records that help messages reach inboxes, whichever provider you use.

Q: Can I switch from .com.pk to .pk later?
A: Yes, but it needs care. Every page must redirect permanently to the new address, Search Console must be updated and email must move without losing messages. If your current domain works well, switching is usually unnecessary. Plan any move carefully and keep the old domain renewed.

A: Yes, we register domains in our clients' own names and emails, never in ours, and set up redirects if you hold both .pk and .com.pk. Business websites start from Rs 40,500, and every project starts with a written quote listing pages, features and timeline.

## One-Page vs Multi-Page Website: Search Visibility, Clarity and Cost for a Small Business
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/one-page-vs-multi-page-website
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: One page vs multi page website: a one-page site puts everything on a single scrolling page, which is quick, cheap and clear for one offer. A multi-page site gives each service its own page, which helps Google show you for more searches. One-page sites start from Rs 22,500; most service businesses need 5 or more pages.
Key points:
- A one-page website suits a single service, an event, a product launch or an ad campaign.
- A multi-page website suits businesses with several services, products or locations.
- Separate pages let Google match each service to the searches people make.
- One-page sites are faster and cheaper to build, but harder to grow later.
- You can start with one page and add pages as the business grows.

Q: Is a one-page website bad for SEO?
A: Not bad, but limited. A one-page site can rank for your business name and its main topic. Because search engines show individual pages, a site with a focused page for each service or area can appear for many more searches. For a single offer, one page is often enough.

Q: When is a one-page website the best choice?
A: It suits a single service or product, an event or launch, an ad campaign, or a new business testing demand on a small budget. With one message and one call to action, visitors know exactly what to do, which often makes one-page sites convert well.

Q: How many pages should a small business website have?
A: Most small service businesses do well with five to eight pages: Home, About, a page for each main service, Contact and frequently asked questions. Add a page only when it has a clear job, such as answering a common question or targeting a search.

Q: Can a one-page website be expanded later?
A: Yes, if it is built on a platform that supports more pages and uses your own domain. Plan which sections will become full pages, and keep the original address working when you expand. One-page builders that cannot add pages usually mean a rebuild.

Q: Is a multi-page website harder for visitors to use?
A: Not if the menu is simple and each page has a clear purpose. Visitors often prefer going straight to the service they need rather than scrolling a long page. Keep the main menu short, link related pages, and make the contact option visible on every page.

## Monthly Website Subscription vs One-Time Build: Total Cost, Ownership and Leaving
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/website-subscription-vs-one-time-build
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Website subscription vs one time build: a subscription spreads the cost into a monthly fee that often includes hosting and updates, but you may not own the site and it can stop when payments stop. A one-time build costs more upfront and you own it. Compare the total over 3 years and read the exit terms.
Key points:
- A subscription lowers the upfront cost but usually costs more over several years.
- Check who owns the domain, design, content and files under each model.
- Many subscriptions end with the site switched off if you stop paying.
- A one-time build is yours; hosting and maintenance are separate, optional costs.
- Compare total cost over three years and the exit terms before signing.

Q: Is renting a website cheaper than buying one?
A: It is cheaper upfront, but often more expensive over several years, because the monthly fee continues for as long as the site runs. Compare the total cost over three years, including setup fees, and check what each option includes before deciding which is cheaper for you.

Q: Do I own a website I pay for monthly?
A: Often not. Many subscription contracts keep the design and files with the provider, and some register the domain in the provider's name. Ask in writing who owns the domain, design, content, photos and files, and what happens to each if you stop paying.

Q: What happens to a subscription website if I cancel?
A: It depends on the contract. Some providers switch the site off, some offer a buy-out fee, some release the domain but not the files, and some charge for leaving before a minimum term. Read the exit terms before signing, and keep the domain in your name.

Q: How do I compare a subscription with a one-time build?
A: Work out the total over 36 months. For the subscription, multiply the monthly fee by 36 and add any setup fee. For the one-time build, add the build price, three years of domain and hosting and any maintenance plan. Then compare ownership and exit terms.

Q: Is maintenance compulsory after a one-time build?
A: No, but some care is needed. Software and plugins need updates, and backups and security matter. You can handle this yourself, hire someone per task or choose a monthly plan. A plan fixes the cost in advance and ensures the work is done regularly.

## Buy Theme vs Custom Design: Licences, Updates, Bloat and When a Ready Theme Fits
URL: https://kambohassociates.com/digital/blog/theme-marketplace-vs-custom-design
Updated: 2026-11-04
Short answer: Buy theme vs custom design comes down to fit and upkeep: a licensed ready theme is quick and affordable when your needs match its layout, but it may carry heavy features, licence limits and update duties. Custom design fits your content exactly and stays lean. Never use a pirated theme; it is 1 of the most common routes for malware.
Key points:
- A licensed theme can save time and money when its layout already fits your content.
- Theme licences usually cover one site; check what the licence allows before buying.
- Many themes bundle page builders and plugins that slow the site and need constant updates.
- Pirated or nulled themes often contain malicious code and receive no security updates.
- Custom design costs more upfront but fits your content and stays faster and easier to maintain.

Q: Is it cheaper to buy a theme than to pay for custom design?
A: Usually, at the start. A licensed theme costs less than a custom design, but setup, adjusting it to your content, and ongoing updates still cost time or money. Bundled plugins can add maintenance work. Compare the total over a few years, not only the purchase price.

Q: Can I use one theme licence on several websites?
A: Usually not. Most theme licences cover one website, and client projects or extra sites need their own licences. Terms differ by seller, so check the exact licence on the seller's page before buying, and keep proof of purchase with your business records.

Q: What is a nulled theme and why is it risky?
A: A nulled theme is a paid theme distributed free without a licence. Such themes often contain hidden code that injects spam, redirects visitors or opens a backdoor for attackers, and they never receive official security updates. Many hacked business websites started with a nulled theme.

Q: Do ready-made themes slow down websites?
A: Multi-purpose themes often load features most sites never use, such as sliders, animations and extra scripts, which slow pages on phones. Choose a lightweight theme, remove unused features and test with PageSpeed Insights. Custom or lean builds usually perform better on Core Web Vitals.

Q: Should the theme licence be in my name?
A: Yes. If a developer builds your site on a paid theme, ask for the licence to be bought in your name or transferred to you. That way you can receive updates and support after the project ends, and you are not dependent on the developer's account.

Q: Does Kamboh Associates Digital use ready-made themes?
A: We use only licensed, well-maintained themes or our own lean builds, never pirated themes, and keep licences in our clients' names. Often we combine a lightweight theme with custom design for key pages. Business websites start from Rs 40,500, with a written quote first.

Short answer: Website retainer vs pay per task: a monthly retainer covers updates, backups, monitoring and a set amount of changes for a fixed fee, which suits sites that change often or must not go down. Pay-per-task suits simple sites that rarely change. Our maintenance plans start from Rs 7,200 a month; tasks outside a plan are quoted first.
Key points:
- A retainer fixes the monthly cost and ensures updates, backups and monitoring happen regularly.
- Pay-per-task means paying only when you request work, but routine care may be forgotten.
- Online stores, booking sites and sites that change weekly usually suit a retainer.
- Small brochure sites that rarely change can suit pay-per-task, if someone still handles updates.
- Put the scope, response times and what is excluded in writing under either model.

Q: Is a monthly website retainer worth it?
A: It is usually worth it for online stores, booking sites and sites that change often or must not go down, because updates, backups and monitoring happen on schedule and the cost is predictable. For a small site that rarely changes, paying per task can cost less.

Q: What does a website maintenance retainer usually include?
A: Most include software and plugin updates, regular backups, security and uptime monitoring, renewal reminders and a set amount of small changes each month. Check the exact list, how extra work is charged, response times and what happens if you cancel, before agreeing.

Q: When is pay-per-task better than a retainer?
A: Pay-per-task suits small brochure sites that change rarely, sites on platforms that handle their own updates, and owners who make most changes themselves. Schedule a regular check at least quarterly, so updates, backups and renewals are not forgotten between tasks.

Q: What is the risk of not having a support plan?
A: The risk is the routine work nobody requests: unpatched plugins, failed backups, missed renewals or forms that stop sending emails. These often surface only when customers complain or the site is hacked, and an emergency fix then costs more than months of routine care.

Q: How do I compare a retainer with paying per task?
